stories.headline: Steelers rout Broncos 27-5 on Black Friday, dropping Denver to 8-3
stories.summary:
The Pittsburgh Steelers beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. The loss dropped Denver to 8-3 on the season.

The Steelers played without quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Wide receiver DK Metcalf scored a touchdown against Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II in the first half. Pittsburgh also intercepted quarterback Bo Nix and returned it for a score.

The Denver Post's postgame grades said the good feeling from the Broncos' previous win over the Raiders disappeared. It said the offensive line struggled throughout the game. The Broncos were also without running back J.K. Dobbins, who was suspended for the game.

Despite the setback, Denver's position in the AFC playoff picture remains strong after 11 weeks of the season.

stories.headline: Broncos seek approval to exceed Capitol mountain view limit at Burnham Yard
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos are seeking an exemption from a view plane restriction that protects mountain views from the Colorado Capitol area. The request relates to the planned stadium at Burnham Yard.

Burnham Yard is the former railyard site where the team plans to build a new stadium. The exemption would allow the structure to rise above the height limit the view plane would otherwise impose.

The Denver Business Journal reported the request in partnership with 9News. The article's available text did not detail the proposed stadium height or a decision timeline.

The request is one of the regulatory steps the Broncos must navigate as the stadium project moves forward.

stories.headline: Nuggets look for fifth straight road win Sunday at Toronto
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets will try to extend a four-game road winning streak when they play the Toronto Raptors on Sunday. The game is the second meeting of the season between the teams.

Denver comes off a 120-101 loss to the Dallas Mavericks in NBA Cup play, in which coach Adelman weighed lineup changes. The Nuggets have otherwise performed well away from home.

Toronto features R.J. Barrett. The Nuggets are led by Nikola Jokic.

stories.headline: Pedestrian killed in hit-and-run near Northeast Park Hill and Central Park
stories.summary:
Denver police are searching for a blue Chevrolet Equinox that struck and killed a pedestrian before fleeing the scene on Friday. The crash happened near North Quebec Street and East 36th Avenue, between the Northeast Park Hill and Central Park neighborhoods, just before noon.

The Colorado Bureau of Investigation issued an alert seeking the vehicle. The crash happened in broad daylight.

Investigators have not released the pedestrian's identity or a description of the driver. Anyone with information is asked to contact Denver police.

The crash was one of several serious traffic incidents in the region over the holiday weekend.

stories.headline: Colorado legislators work toward Medicaid reforms as costs outpace new tax revenue
stories.summary:
Colorado lawmakers are working on Medicaid reforms while acknowledging that the voter-approved graduated income tax, Amendment 87, will not by itself solve the program's financial pressures. The legislature's Medicaid Commission approved about 60 recommendations, after considering nearly 130, to improve sustainability, administrative efficiency and fiscal oversight.

The recommendations are a guide for future legislation, administrative changes and budget decisions in the 2027 session, not enacted laws. About 26% of Coloradans receive care through Medicaid. The program was $157.9 million over budget in fiscal year 2025-26, and the 2026-27 overrun is projected to exceed $443 million.

The Department of Health Care Policy and Financing's general fund appropriation rose from $2.6 billion in fiscal 2021 to $5.3 billion in fiscal 2026. Most of the increase came in long-term care, acute care and behavioral health.

State officials expect more than $2 billion in added revenue from Amendment 87. Rep. Kyle Brown, D-Louisville, said spending is expected to run $1 billion over this year's Medicaid budget, and some lawmakers say rising costs could consume the new revenue.

stories.headline: Colorado certifies 2026 general election; Laubacher defeats Boebert
stories.summary:
Colorado officials certified the 2026 general election, which Democrats dominated, winning several battleground congressional districts. Secretary of State Jena Griswold's office said the results are official after postelection audits and county canvass certifications.

In the closest congressional race, Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated U.S. Rep. Lauren Boebert, 48.79% to 47.87%. Democrat Jessica Killin won the 5th District over Rep. Jeff Crank, and Democrat Manny Rutinel beat Rep. Gabe Evans in the 8th. Rep. Jeff Hurd's 3rd District seat was the only Republican seat that did not flip.

Sen. John Hickenlooper was reelected with 60.5%. Attorney General Phil Weiser won the governor's race with 61.13% to Republican Victor Marx's 33.21%. Jeffco Clerk Amanda Gonzalez was elected secretary of state.

Turnout was 66.68% of 4.1 million active voters, with 94.8% of ballots cast by mail. Unaffiliated voters made up 45.88% of accepted ballots, Democrats 28.64% and Republicans 23.78%.

stories.headline: Data from about 100,000 users accessed in myColorado app breach
stories.summary:
About 100,000 Coloradans' data, including photos of passports, vehicle registrations and insurance cards, was accessed in a cybersecurity breach of the myColorado digital ID app. State officials shut the app down ahead of Thanksgiving travel.

The Governor's Office of Information Technology said automated threat detection flagged apparent unauthorized activity on Nov. 18. The affected material was in the app's "myCards and Documents" section, which holds PDFs and photos uploaded by users. Payment information was not involved.

The estimate could change as staff match accessed documents to individual users. About 2.1 million Coloradans use the app. OIT will begin notifying affected users Friday.

The office is testing security enhancements and hopes to restore the app next week, spokesperson Erin Jeffreys said. State Chief Information Officer Sarah Tuneberg said the team is working to verify every affected individual.

stories.headline: Woman killed in Thanksgiving night crash involving elk near Meeker
stories.summary:
A 63-year-old woman died in a crash involving an elk and two vehicles on Thanksgiving night in Rio Blanco County, the Colorado State Patrol said. The crash happened about 9:45 p.m. Thursday on Colorado Highway 13 near milepost 37, north of Meeker.

Investigators said a southbound Ford F-150 struck an elk crossing the highway. The impact pushed the elk into the northbound lane, where an oncoming Subaru Forester hit it. The Subaru then traveled off the right side of the road, and its driver was pronounced dead at the scene.

The 43-year-old driver of the Ford and three passengers were treated for minor injuries. The crash remains under investigation.

The State Patrol noted that November is the top month for wildlife crashes as animals move to wintering grounds. It urged drivers to stay at or below the speed limit, scan for movement and eye shine, and drive straight through an animal rather than swerve if a collision is unavoidable.

stories.headline: Denver police seek help solving year-old shooting death of Miguel Romero
stories.summary:
The Denver Police Department is asking for public help in solving the killing of Miguel Romero, 42, a year after his death. Romero was shot on Nov. 29, 2025, at about 5:45 p.m. in the 3000 block of South Winona Court, near South Sheridan Boulevard and West Hampden Avenue.

Police said the shooting followed a traffic dispute. The suspect is described as an English-speaking Hispanic man, possibly in his mid-20s.

He was driving a white or light-colored compact pickup truck similar to a Chevy Colorado. The truck may have yellow or orange lights on the front in addition to the headlights.

Detectives are actively working the case. Anyone with information can call Metro Denver Crime Stoppers at 720-913-7867.

stories.headline: Wax Trax hit by vehicle for second time this year; owner urges safer street design
stories.summary:
The Denver record store Wax Trax was struck by a vehicle for the second time in about six months. Denver police said a driver heading south on Washington Street failed to stop at a red light, and a vehicle heading west on 13th Avenue was then hit. The at-fault vehicle spun and hit two pedestrians, and the second vehicle lost control and struck the building.

No one was seriously hurt, and the at-fault driver was cited for running the red light. Co-owner Pete Stidman said his 82-year-old father, a Wax Trax founder, had walked through the spot minutes earlier.

Stidman said barriers and bollards the city added are not enough, because a small SUV went through a bollard. He argued the street is designed for speed and wants narrower lanes and speed tables.

The Denver Department of Transportation and Infrastructure said it placed a jersey barrier as a temporary measure and is considering near- and longer-term treatments.

stories.headline: Study finds Colorado losing company headquarters at twice the rate it gains them
stories.summary:
A Common Sense Institute study found Colorado is losing corporate headquarters at twice the rate it is acquiring them. The Greenwood Village-based think tank said departures have set a seven-year trend of losses. Over the past four years, 27 operations left while 13 arrived.

The study appears to have been prompted by Palantir Technologies' move to the Miami area. The company had been the highest-valued in Colorado history. It was the most prominent of at least 24 companies to leave since 2023.

Gov. Jared Polis, who opposed Amendment 87, warned that the new graduated income tax would accelerate an "exodus" unless policymakers act. He said about 160 companies have come to Colorado since 2019, creating nearly 43,000 net new jobs.

An economic index released last week put Colorado 44th in tax competitiveness, an 11-place drop. Backers say the $2 billion to $2.7 billion in new annual revenue will fund schools, healthcare and childcare.

stories.headline: Colorado mountain real estate cools as ski season begins
stories.summary:
Colorado's mountain real estate market is cooling as ski season starts, with October sales slipping across much of the Mountain West, according to the Colorado Association of Realtors. Statewide closed sales fell about 19%, while prices barely moved and sellers made the adjustments.

In Summit County, single-family sales dropped about 16% and the average price slid 2.5% to about $2.28 million. Condo inventory jumped 31% to 593 listings, an 8.2-month supply, and the average condo price fell 17%. Grand County listings rose 11% to 652 as pending sales fell more than 19%.

Steamboat Springs had 20 single-family sales with the median price up 3% to about $2.2 million. In Telluride, San Miguel County posted $65.8 million across 39 transactions, down 17% in dollars.

Historic flooding beginning Nov. 1 damaged bridges and roads in La Plata County and Pagosa Springs. Mortgage rates eased from 7.32% to 7.18% between Oct. 22 and Nov. 5, according to Freddie Mac.

weather.notable: Nearly 5 degrees above the average high for this time of year.

topStory.headline: Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade Rescheduled to Saturday After Storm, Adds LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor
topStory.summary:
Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade, postponed for the first time in its history because of a powerful storm, is set to step off Saturday, Nov. 28, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding struck the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day, and the National Weather Service issued a high-wind warning for potentially damaging gusts. Concerns about whether the giant balloons could fly safely led Macy's to move the event after consulting city and agency partners.

Will Coss, vice president and executive producer of Macy's Studios, told The Associated Press the Saturday parade will largely match the one planned for Thursday, with the same balloons, floats and 1,000 clowns. He said 90 to 95 percent of bands, performance groups and celebrity talent were able to adjust their plans. The lineup includes Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Queen Latifah, Keke Palmer, JoJo, RAYE, Mckenna Grace, and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, along with a Dolly Parton tribute led by Megan Hilty. Singer Gloria Gaynor and actor-rapper LL Cool J have been added, and the casts of "Wicked," "Hamilton" and "The Rocky Horror Show" are also slated to perform.

The delay forced some participants to scramble. The Pride of Pearland Marching Band from Pearland High School in Texas raised $350,000 through a fundraiser to extend its stay, while the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign's Marching Illini raised funds to cover roughly $175,000 in additional costs. Broadway productions had to determine whether casts could handle both the parade and Saturday matinees hours later. The University of Alabama's Million Dollar Band will not take part, as it will return home to play at a football game.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledged the inconvenience but said the postponement was necessary to protect participants and spectators. The parade has been modified for weather before, including in 1971 when balloons were grounded, but it had never been moved to a different date. Meteorologist Matt Wunsch said Saturday morning should be dry, with sustained winds of about 10 to 15 mph and gusts that could reach about 25 mph, well below Thursday's conditions.

NBC and Peacock will broadcast the parade from 8:30 a.m. to noon Eastern, with a Spanish-language simulcast on Telemundo, followed by a rebroadcast of the National Dog Show, now in its 25th year. Coss said organizers see the rescheduled event as adding to the milestone, calling it the first parade shifted from its original date. Organizers expect the parade to reach a couple of million people.
